steps.title: Secure your mailbox first
steps.body:
Before anything else: turn on two-factor authentication (2FA) on your email account. This is the first, most important step — your mailbox is often the key to all your other accounts (via 'forgot password').

In Gmail this is under Settings > Security > 2-Step Verification.

steps.title: Writing professional emails
steps.body:
For job applications, work, or official matters:

  • A clear subject line, not 'hi' or 'question'
  • Short, direct text — get to the point quickly
  • Check your automatic signature (name, role, phone number)
  • Read your email once before sending

steps.title: Spotting phishing starts here
steps.body:
A large share of phishing arrives by email. Even while reading, watch for:

  • Does the sender address really match, or does it just look similar?
  • Is there pressure to act ('take action right now')?
  • Does the email ask you to log in via a link instead of opening the app/website yourself?

We'll go deeper into this later (Safety module) — but the sooner you recognize the pattern, the better.

lessons.title: Attachments and sharing via the cloud

steps.title: Sending attachments
steps.body: Click the paperclip icon 📎 to add a file. For large files (photos, videos), Gmail often automatically offers a Google Drive link instead of a direct attachment.

steps.title: Why a link beats an attachment
steps.body: Sharing a document someone needs to respond to or work on? Send a share link (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive) instead of an attachment. Benefit: everyone works on the same, current version, instead of getting three separate files named 'document_final_v3.docx'.

steps.title: Setting permissions when sharing
steps.body: When sharing a link you can usually choose: view only, comment, or edit. Never grant more access than needed, and never share sensitive documents with 'anyone with the link' — pick specific people instead.

steps.title: Exercise
steps.body: Try sharing a file in Google Drive and setting the permissions to 'view only'.

steps.title: Searching efficiently
steps.body: Use quotation marks to search for an exact phrase, for example "best laptop 2026". Want to exclude a site or word? Type -word. This saves you a lot of scrolling through irrelevant results.

steps.title: Privacy settings in your browser
steps.body:
Go to your browser's settings (in Chrome: the three dots top right > Settings > Privacy and security). There you can:

  • Block third-party cookies
  • Manage your browsing and search history
  • Review site permissions (location, camera, microphone) per site

steps.title: Using multiple tabs smartly
steps.body: Open a link in a new tab by clicking it with your scroll wheel (or right-click > 'Open in new tab'). This keeps your current page open while you check something else. Ctrl+Tab quickly switches between tabs.

lessons.title: Video calling for work and personal life

steps.title: More than WhatsApp
steps.body: For work you'll often use Microsoft Teams, Zoom, or Google Meet instead of WhatsApp. The principle is the same: turn on your camera and microphone, and open the link or meeting at the agreed time.

steps.title: Making a professional impression
steps.body:
• Check your background (or use a virtual background/blur)
  • Mute your microphone when you're not speaking
  • Make sure you have good lighting — don't sit with your back to a window

steps.title: Sharing your screen
steps.body: Want to show a document or presentation? During the call, click 'Share screen' and choose the window or screen you want to show. Remember to stop sharing when you're done.
